findings.title: Strict pyright will reject bare `np.ndarray` annotations in new confidence tests
findings.description: Description: `tests/core_model/test_confidence.py:69` and `tests/core_model/test_confidence.py:73` annotate helpers as bare `np.ndarray`, while NumPy's `ndarray` is generic and the rest of the suite uses parameterized forms such as `NDArray[np.float64]` / `NDArray[np.bool_]` in `tests/core_model/test_labels.py:49-52`. The configured `[tool.pyright]` block in `pyproject.toml` enables `typeCheckingMode = "strict"`, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:33` runs `uv run pyright`; the Additional Rules make zero strict-pyright errors a merge blocker. These annotations should trigger `reportMissingTypeArgument` and fail CI. Use `NDArray[np.float64]` and `NDArray[np.bool_]`, or fully parameterized `np.ndarray[...]`, for these helper return types.

findings.title: SignalEvent can raise AttributeError instead of InvalidSignalError for a malformed Timestamp meaning
findings.description: Description: `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:76-80` assumes `self.time.meaning.value` is available when building the error message. However, `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/timestamps.py:55-58` only type-annotates `meaning` and range-checks `ns`; it does not validate that `meaning` is a `TimeMeaning` at runtime. A caller can construct `Timestamp(100, "available_at")` or `Timestamp(100, None)` and then pass it to `SignalEvent`; the `is not TimeMeaning.AVAILABLE_AT` branch is taken and `.value` raises `AttributeError`, violating D5's contract that anything other than `AVAILABLE_AT` raises `InvalidSignalError`. The rejection cases in `tests/core_model/test_signals.py:80-88` cover valid enum alternatives and a float `ns`, but not a non-enum `meaning`. Validate `time.meaning` as a `TimeMeaning` before comparing, and add a regression test for a string/`None` meaning.

findings.title: Supported iterable/set inputs are published with tuple/frozenset-only type contracts
findings.description: Description: `SignalSequence`'s docstring says the constructor accepts any iterable of events, but `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/signals.py:102` declares `events: tuple[SignalEvent, ...]`; the positive test at `tests/core_model/test_signals.py:122` therefore needs a `pyright: ignore` to pass a list. The same mismatch appears in `Declarations`: `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/declarations.py:188-189` declares tuple-only fields while `tests/core_model/test_declarations.py:192` passes lists with a type ignore, and in `LabelVocabulary`: `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/labels.py:50` declares `frozenset[int]` while the comment at `src/manta_trading_engine/core_model/labels.py:55` and test at `tests/core_model/test_labels.py:66` explicitly support a `set`. These are valid runtime inputs, not invalid-input probes, so the public annotations should accept `Iterable[...]` / `set[int] | frozenset[int]` and normalize internally, or the docs/runtime behavior should be tightened to match the static contract.
